import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.5

by S. I. Adian

Is it true that an arbitrary finitely presented group has either polynomial or exponential growth?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.5»

open GromovPolynomialGrowth

/-- A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a free group on finitely many generators
modulo the normal closure of finitely many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (R : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), R.Finite ∧
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup R)

/-- A group has exponential growth if, for some finite generating set, its word-ball counting
function is bounded below by $c^n$ for some real number $c > 1$. -/
def HasExponentialGrowth (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (S : Set G), S.Finite ∧ Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ ∧
    ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, c ^ n ≤ (GrowthFunction S n : ℝ)

/--
Is it true that every finitely presented group has either polynomial or exponential growth?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFinitelyPresented G →
      HasPolynomialGrowth G ∨ HasExponentialGrowth G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.5»

Used the repository's existing `GromovPolynomialGrowth.HasPolynomialGrowth` predicate for polynomial growth.
Modeled exponential growth by existence of a finite generating set `S` and a real `c > 1` such that `c ^ n ≤ GrowthFunction S n` for every natural-number radius `n`.
Quantified over `G : Type` with a `Group G` instance, following nearby Kourovka repository style, and placed the unknown yes/no answer before the universal assertion.

    ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, c ^ n ≤ (GrowthFunction S n : ℝ)

/--
Is it true that every finitely presented group has either polynomial or exponential growth?
-/

theorem parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFinitelyPresented G →
      HasPolynomialGrowth G ∨ HasExponentialGrowth G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.5»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.5

by S. I. Adian

b) Is it true that an arbitrary finitely presented group has either polynomial or
exponential growth?

In other words, does no finitely presented group have intermediate growth? Part a) of the
problem asked the same question for finitely generated groups; it was answered in the
negative by Grigorchuk and is not part of the statement formalized here.

A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to the quotient of a free group on finitely
many generators by the normal closure of a finite set of relators. Growth is measured by the
growth function $\gamma_S(n)$ of a finite generating set $S$, which counts the elements of the
group that are products of at most $n$ elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$. Whether the growth is
polynomial or exponential does not depend on the choice of the finite generating set $S$. The
group has polynomial growth if $\gamma_S(n) \leq C n^d$ for all $n > 0$ and some constants
$C > 0$, $d \in \mathbb{N}$, and exponential growth if $\gamma_S(n) \geq c^n$ for all $n$ and
some constant $c > 1$ (equivalently, the growth rate $\lim_n \gamma_S(n)^{1/n}$, which exists
since $\gamma_S$ is submultiplicative, is strictly greater than $1$).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.5»

open GromovPolynomialGrowth

/-- A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to $\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R
\rangle$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and some finite set $R$ of relators, that is, to the quotient
of the free group on $n$ generators by the normal closure of $R$. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)

/-- A group has exponential growth if there exists a finite generating set $S$ whose growth
function $\gamma_S$ is bounded below by a geometric sequence $c^n$ with $c > 1$. Equivalently,
the growth rate $\lim_n \gamma_S(n)^{1/n}$ is strictly greater than $1$. -/
def HasExponentialGrowth (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (S : Set G), S.Finite ∧ Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ ∧
    ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, c ^ n ≤ (GrowthFunction S n : ℝ)

/-- A group presented by finitely many generators and finitely many relators is finitely
presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} {rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))}
    (h : rels.Finite) : IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨n, rels, h, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- The free group on finitely many generators is finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_freeGroup (n : ℕ) : IsFinitelyPresented (FreeGroup (Fin n)) :=
  ⟨n, ∅, Set.finite_empty, ⟨(QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq
    (le_bot_iff.mp (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (Set.empty_subset _)))).trans
    (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := FreeGroup (Fin n)))⟩⟩

/-- A group of exponential growth is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem HasExponentialGrowth.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : HasExponentialGrowth G) : Group.FG G :=
  ⟨⟨h.choose_spec.1.toFinset, by simpa using h.choose_spec.2.1⟩⟩

/-- A finite group does not have exponential growth. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_hasExponentialGrowth_of_finite {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] :
    ¬ HasExponentialGrowth G := by
  rintro ⟨S, -, -, c, hc, h⟩
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := pow_unbounded_of_one_lt (Nat.card G : ℝ) hc
  refine absurd ((h n).trans ?_) (not_le.mpr hn)
  exact_mod_cast Set.ncard_le_card _

/--
Is it true that an arbitrary finitely presented group has either polynomial or exponential
growth?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.5».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFinitelyPresented G →
      HasPolynomialGrowth G ∨ HasExponentialGrowth G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.5»

set of relators `rels` in a free group of finite rank. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)

/-- A group has exponential growth if there is a finite generating set `S` whose growth
function is bounded below by $c^n$ for some $c > 1$. -/
def HasExponentialGrowth (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (S : Set G), S.Finite ∧ Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ ∧
    ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, c ^ n ≤ (GrowthFunction S n : ℝ)

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) :
    Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  haveI : Group.FG (PresentedGroup rels) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨_, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of rels, Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.surjective

/-- Free groups of finite rank are finitely presented. -/

    le_bot_iff.mp (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (Set.empty_subset _))

  exact absurd (h n) (not_le.mpr (this.trans_lt hn))

/-!
# Conjecture 4.5

by S. I. Adian

b) Is it true that an arbitrary finitely presented group has either polynomial or
exponential growth?

Part a) of the problem, the same question for finitely generated groups, was answered
in the negative by Grigorchuk and is not part of this statement.

A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a quotient of a free group of finite
rank by the normal closure of a finite set of relators. The growth of a finitely generated
group $G$ is measured by the growth function $\gamma_S(n)$ of a finite generating set $S$,
which counts the elements of $G$ that are products of at most $n$ elements of
$S \cup S^{-1}$. Whether the growth is polynomial ($\gamma_S(n) \le C n^d$) or exponential
($\gamma_S(n) \ge c^n$ for some $c > 1$) does not depend on the choice of $S$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open GromovPolynomialGrowth

namespace Kourovka.«4.5»

/-- A group $G$ is finitely presented if there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a finite set of
relators $R \subseteq F_n$ in the free group on $n$ generators such that $G$ is isomorphic
to $\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$, the quotient of $F_n$ by the normal closure
of $R$. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- A group has exponential growth if there is a finite generating set $S$ and a constant
$c > 1$ such that the growth function of $S$ satisfies $\gamma_S(n) \ge c^n$ for all $n$.

For a finitely generated group this does not depend on the choice of the finite generating
set. Since $\gamma_S$ is submultiplicative, it is equivalent to the growth rate
$\lim_{n \to \infty} \gamma_S(n)^{1/n}$ being greater than $1$. -/
def HasExponentialGrowth (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (S : Set G), S.Finite ∧ Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ ∧
    ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, c ^ n ≤ (GrowthFunction S n : ℝ)

/-- A group given by a finite presentation is finitely presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} {rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))}
    (h : rels.Finite) : IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨n, rels, h, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) : Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  haveI : Group.FG (PresentedGroup rels) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨_, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of rels, Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.symm.toMonoidHom) e.symm.surjective

/--
b) Is it true that an arbitrary finitely presented group has either polynomial or
exponential growth?

That is, does every finitely presented group $G$ have a finite generating set $S$ such
that the growth function $\gamma_S$ either is bounded above by a polynomial $C n^d$
(for $n > 0$) or is bounded below by $c^n$ for some $c > 1$? Equivalently, is there no
finitely presented group of intermediate growth?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.5».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFinitelyPresented G →
      HasPolynomialGrowth G ∨ HasExponentialGrowth G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.5»

  ⟨n, rels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩
